newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: YPF contests order to cap all wells in spill area.
newsitem.headline: YPF contests order to cap all wells in spill area.

text.p: Argentina's oil giant YPF SA said Thursday it challenged in court an order from the government to cap all of its 112 wells in two oil fields in Patagonia due to recent spills.
"We sought Wednesday a court order in Buenos Aires to see whether the government has the right to ask for the closures," YPF's vice-President for Upstream Marcelo Guiscardo told Reuters.

"We had closed all the (52) wells in Desfiladero Bayo oil field," he said in a telephone interview from the town of Rincon de los Sauces, Neuquen province, some 1,300 km (850 miles) south west of Buenos Aires.
"But in Puerto Molina (field) we only capped seven, not the 60 the Energy Secretariat had requested, as we deemed there is no technical reason to close the rest."

Guiscardo said YPF only closed the wells it deemed could pose a risk to the population or the environment. Rincon de los Sauces was affected by recent leaks of crude oil into the Colorado River, its main source of water.
He acknowledged the firm's decision may not please authorities but added YPF considers the government has "no justified reason" to order the closing of all the wells.
Guiscardo said the 59 capped wells represented for YPF a loss of less than one percent of its total output or just between $50,000 and $70,000 per day.
He added that in three spills in February 15 and March 6 and 7 only a total of 25 cubic meters of oil were spilled into the river and that the company had already cleaned 10.
Nevertheless Neuquen authorities said thousands of cubic meters of oil leaked into the Colorado.
Guiscardo said YPF has set a 60-day deadline to fix the broken pipes but work may be completed even sooner.
